events.text: A face you do not know at all stands at the crossroads where, in your memory, nobody ever stood. People call them by a name you have never heard, and they are already somebody here. Something you changed made room for them.

effects.log: You ask, and listen, and come away knowing less than you thought you knew about this world.
You keep clear. It is the first time in two lives you have had to guess.

events.text: A small house you remember as ashes is standing, and doing well. In this life nobody burned it. The people in it have no idea they were supposed to be gone by now.

effects.log: You stand at its gate for a long time. A child asks if you are lost. You are, a little.
You walk past. Some things are better not looked at too closely.

events.text: The year your memory calls quiet is not quiet at all: a quarrel between two houses that never quarrelled breaks out on the roads, and nobody in it is following the story you know.

effects.log: You stay out of it. For once you cannot tell how it ends.

choices.text: Lend a hand to the weaker side

effects.log: You lend a hand. Neither side thanks you, and both remember you.

events.text: A letter arrives for you from someone who, in the life you remember, died before you were ten. They are alive, and they write as if they had always known you.

effects.log: You write back. It takes three tries to get the first line right.
You burn it. Your hands are not quite steady.

events.text: A threat the old timeline never had is gathering in the next valley: a gang that should have scattered years ago, held together by a leader who rose in the space you left.

ok.log: You break them in one night. The valley never learns how close it came.

fail.log: They are stronger than a thing that should not exist has any right to be. You get away.

choices.text: Warn the valley and leave it to them

effects.log: You send word. The valley sends men. It is enough, mostly.

events.text: An old master who has been watching the children train stops beside you, takes your wrist and turns it over as if reading something written there. "Who taught you to hold your breath like that?" the master asks.

effects.log: You let the master see a little more than you should.
You shrug and say you copied the older ones. The master lets go of your wrist slowly.

events.text: A master drops a pebble from the top of the wall without warning, aimed at your head. Your hand is already there to catch it, and everyone sees the hand was there first.

effects.log: You toss the pebble back, and the master catches it, smiling for the first time in years.
You drop it at once, as if it burned, and pretend to be frightened. Some of them believe it.

events.text: A master sets a board between you and plays a game of strategy for an hour, saying nothing. At the end the master looks at the board, then at you. "Again," the master says. "And this time, play like yourself."

effects.log: You play like yourself. The master stops looking at the board and only looks at you.
You play like a clever child and lose on purpose. It is the hardest game of the day.

events.text: Two senior disciples of a great house arrive at your door with gifts and polite faces. Their house has heard about you, they say, and would like to raise you as one of its own.

effects.log: You go with them.

choices.text: Refuse, as politely as they asked

effects.log: You refuse, and they go, and the gifts go with them. The talk dies down a little.

events.text: A house sends its own elder this time, which it does not do for ordinary children. "Whatever you are," the elder says quietly, "you will be safer inside our walls than outside them."

effects.log: You take it. Inside the walls, people stop asking where you came from.
You stay outside. The elder nods as if that, too, told him something.

events.text: The rumour has reached a great house: a child who fights like an old master. A letter arrives with its seal, offering a place, a teacher and a room of your own.

effects.log: You accept. The house is glad to have found you before anyone else did.
You send it back. A seal like that does not often hear no.

events.text: {npc} has been asking about you for a year. Tonight {he} stops asking and comes in person, alone, with a weapon {he} does not bother to hide. Somebody has decided you are too dangerous to be allowed to grow up.

ok.log: {npc} did not expect a child to fight like that. {He} goes back the way {he} came, more slowly than {he} arrived.

fail.log: You lose, and live, because {he} is called away before {he} can finish. You know {he} will try again.

choices.text: Run, and keep running until morning

effects.log: You run, and keep running. By morning you are a long way from where anyone expects you to be.

choices.text: Talk: tell {him} you are only a child

effects.log: You talk, and keep talking, and at the end {npc} is no longer sure of anything. {He} leaves.

events.text: {npc} waits for you on the road home, where the trees are thick and nobody passes after dark. {He} does not say why. {He} does not need to.

ok.log: {npc} goes down. When {he} gets up {he} walks away without looking back.

fail.log: {npc} leaves you in the ditch and goes. You were lucky {he} was in a hurry.

choices.text: Go back the way you came

effects.log: You go back. You take another road home, and another the next day.
{npc} laughs, but answers more than {he} meant to. You let {him} go and remember the name.

events.text: A cup of tea set out for you smells wrong, and when you look up, {npc} across the room is watching to see if you will lift it.

ok.log: {npc} was ready for poison, not for you. {He} leaves with a great deal to think about.

fail.log: {npc} gets the better of you and slips away. The tea goes untouched.

choices.text: Knock the cup over and leave

effects.log: You knock it over, apologise and leave. {npc} does not follow, this time.

choices.text: Pour it out slowly and talk

effects.log: You pour it out in front of {him}, and then you talk. {npc} decides you are more trouble alive than dead.

events.text: You find {npc} where your list said {he} would be. {He} does not know you; in this life you have never met. {He} only sees someone looking at {him} the way nobody has looked at {him} before.

ok.log: It is over between you and {npc}. You stand over {him}, and two lives come to rest.

fail.log: {npc} is stronger than your memory said. You come away with nothing but the knowledge, and {he} knows your face now.

effects.log: You find the people who should know, and you tell them, with proof only a ghost could have.
You turn and walk away before {he} can ask who you are.

events.text: {npc} is older than in your memory, and kinder to the people around {him}, which is somehow worse. {He} looks up from {his} work and asks what you want.

ok.log: It is over between you and {npc}. You stand over {him}, and two lives come to rest.

fail.log: {npc} is stronger than your memory said. You come away with nothing but the knowledge, and {he} knows your face now.

effects.log: You do not draw. You go to {his} house instead, and you tell it everything.
You say you have the wrong person. You leave {him} to the people {he} is kind to.

events.text: {npc} is holding court at a long table, surrounded by people who owe {him} things. When you walk in, the talk stops, though nobody there could say why.

choices.text: Call {him} out in front of them all

ok.log: It is over between you and {npc}. You stand over {him}, and two lives come to rest.

fail.log: {npc} is stronger than your memory said. You come away with nothing but the knowledge, and {he} knows your face now.

effects.log: You say what {he} did, in front of everyone {he} owes. You watch the table empty around {him}.
You sit, and eat, and leave. {npc} watches you go and never learns why {his} hands were shaking.

events.text: On a bridge in the rain, {npc} and you meet in the middle, and neither steps aside. In the other life this bridge was where it all began.

ok.log: It is over between you and {npc}. You stand over {him}, and two lives come to rest.

fail.log: {npc} is stronger than your memory said. You come away with nothing but the knowledge, and {he} knows your face now.

effects.log: You step aside, and you go to {his} house with what you know, and that is how it ends instead.
You step aside. It costs you more than any fight.

events.text: An elder of the house you were born into to destroy sits with you through a fever, all night, and in the morning pretends it was nothing. In your other life this house gave you no kindness at all.

effects.log: You let it in. It is harder to hate a place that has held your hand.
You remember. You thank the elder, and you go on counting the house's weaknesses.

events.text: The house celebrates a festival, and somebody saves you the best seat without being asked. Everyone is laughing, and for an hour you forget who you were.

effects.log: You laugh with them. You do not remember the last time you laughed like that, in either life.

choices.text: Use the hour to look around

effects.log: While they laugh you learn where the house keeps its records, and its keys.

events.text: A junior of the house looks up to you as if you were the sun. You remember this junior from the other life: in that life they died defending the house against you.

effects.log: You decide nothing will happen to this one. Not this time.
You harden your heart. You will have to, if you mean to do what you came to do.

events.text: Late at night you overhear the head of the house talking about you, and every word is pride. The house thinks you are its future.

choices.text: Want to be what they think you are

effects.log: You lie awake wanting it, and that frightens you more than anything has in years.
You let them think it. A house that trusts you is a house you can break.

events.text: It is all ready: the records, the keys, the ones who will turn when you ask. One word from you and the house that killed you comes down from within, and nobody will ever know whose hand it was.

effects.log: You say it.
You put it away. Not yet. Perhaps not ever.

events.text: The night is right, the guards are the ones you chose, and the gate is open. Everything you have done in this life has led you to this courtyard.

effects.log: You bring it down.

choices.text: Close the gate and go to bed

effects.log: You close the gate yourself, and sleep badly, and wake still one of them.

events.text: Enemies come for the house at last: the same ones, you realise, who once came with you at their head. The house turns to you to lead the defence.

effects.log: You stand for it.

choices.text: Stand aside and remember who you were

effects.log: You stand aside. The house holds without you, barely, and looks at you differently after.

events.text: The head of the house is dying, and asks for you, and only you. "Look after them," the head says. "They are yours now."

effects.log: You promise. You mean it more than anything you swore in the other life.
You say nothing, and the head dies not knowing. You are not sure what you would have said.

events.text: Someone has put it together: the arts you should not know, the places you should not have known to look. They come for you at dawn with the whole house behind them.

effects.log: You go over the wall.

choices.text: Stand in the courtyard and tell them the truth

effects.log: You tell them all of it.

events.text: An old elder of the house calls you in alone and closes the door. "I fought you once," the elder says. "Long ago, in a life that should not exist. I know your stance."

choices.text: Run before the door opens again

effects.log: You run.

choices.text: Sit down and tell the elder everything

effects.log: You sit down, and you tell everything, and then the elder calls in the others.

events.text: The gate of the house you once led is peeling, and half its name has fallen off the board. Children in the street laugh at the three disciples sweeping its yard. None of them know you; none of them could.

effects.log: You pick up a broom.

choices.text: Laugh with the street and walk on

effects.log: You walk on.

events.text: You find it at last: smaller than you remember, poorer than you could have imagined, its hall half empty. A rival house's disciples pass its gate and spit, and nobody inside dares answer.

effects.log: You knock. A tired old caretaker lets you in, mostly because nobody else is coming.
You leave. Some things are allowed to end.

events.text: Behind the third pillar of the back hall there was once a hidden room. Your hands remember the loose stone before your eyes find it. It is still there, and nobody in this life has ever opened it.

effects.log: You open it in front of them all.
You take back the silver that was once yours.

events.text: The house is selling its last old furniture to pay for rice. You stop them at the old cabinet: the false bottom is still there, and under it the seal of the house as it was.

effects.log: You give it to the house.
You keep the silver and give them the seal.

events.text: The house's own art has been lost for three generations: what the disciples train is a shadow of it. You know it as well as your own hands, because once they were your hands.

effects.log: You write all night.

choices.text: Teach it with your own hands

effects.log: You teach it, form by form.

events.text: A junior is trying to make sense of a manual with half its pages gone, and getting it wrong in exactly the way that will one day crack a meridian.

effects.log: You fill them in, from memory.

choices.text: Show the junior the right way

effects.log: You show the junior the right way, and then the others.

events.text: A rival house holds the deeds to the house's land and means to take it at the end of the season. The debt is real, and so is the deadline.

effects.log: You pay it in full.

choices.text: Win the land back field by field

effects.log: You start with the nearest field.

events.text: The moneylenders come to the house's gate every month now, and every month the old caretaker apologises to them. You are tired of hearing the apology.

effects.log: You pay them off.

choices.text: Earn it back the hard way

effects.log: You go to work.

events.text: The rival house that has laughed at yours for two generations sends a challenge: an exchange match, in front of the whole town, meant to finish what is left of its name.

effects.log: You decline. The town laughs again, but more quietly.

events.text: The rival house's best young fighter stands at the gate and calls the house's name like an insult. Behind you, the juniors are watching to see what you will do.

effects.log: You close the gate. The juniors say nothing, which is worse.

events.text: The hall is full again. The name on the gate has been painted fresh. A child in the street points at the house and says to another, "I am going to train there when I grow up."

choices.text: Take a seat at its table

effects.log: You take the seat they have been keeping for you.
You walk on, and nobody knows, and it is enough.

events.text: The rival house sends a gift to yours, for the first time in living memory, and a letter that is almost respectful. The old caretaker reads it three times and then cries.

effects.log: You stay.
You leave it in good hands.

events.text: Two strangers at the next table are arguing about you without knowing you can hear. Both of them use the new name. It sounds strange, and it sounds like you.

effects.log: You do not correct them.
You lean over and tell them your name, the one you already had.

events.text: A child runs up to you in the market and asks, out of breath, if you are really the one people are talking about. The child uses the new name, as if it had always been yours.

effects.log: You say yes.
You give the child the name you prefer, and a coin to remember it by.

events.text: A storyteller in the square is telling what you did, and getting most of it wrong, and at the end gives the hero of the story a name. Everyone in the square turns to look at you.

effects.log: You nod to the storyteller, and the square cheers.
You tell the storyteller, kindly, that the hero has a name already.
